title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for history of deep vein thrombosis.

HPI
The patient is a 79-year-old female presenting today for a routine follow-up regarding a prior deep vein thrombosis of the right leg. She originally experienced this condition two years ago. She reports that the course of treatment was completed and she has since had the condition resolved. She currently reports no pain, swelling, or discomfort in the right leg. She denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, or calf tenderness. She states she feels well and is seeking a baseline evaluation.

Medication List
1. Multivitamin daily
2. Vitamin D3 supplement daily

Review of Systems
The patient denies fever, chills, weight loss, or night sweats. She reports no shortness of breath or cough. She denies any recent swelling or redness in her lower extremities. She denies joint pain or muscle weakness.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives at home with her spouse. She enjoys gardening and walking for exercise. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension and stroke. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Height: 5'4"
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Right lower extremity shows no signs of edema, erythema, or warmth. Full range of motion is intact.

Assessment
1. History of deep vein thrombosis of the right leg. The condition is resolved and stable.

Plan
1. Continue to monitor for any symptoms of recurrence.
2. Patient advised to seek immediate medical attention if she develops sudden swelling or localized pain in the lower extremity.
3. Follow up in 6 months for a routine check.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: A DVT that resolved after completed treatment: personal history, Z86.718 (no HCC).

distractors.why: There is no current clot: code the history.
